definition: A piece of an existing recording placed in a new work. The word for the digital process is credited to the Fairlight's founders.
Part of an existing song performed and recorded again, with none of the original audio, as with the Kraftwerk melody on "Planet Rock" and the bassline of "Rapper's Delight".
A new recording of a whole existing song that keeps its basic melody and character.
An existing recording with sounds added, changed or removed.
Two or more sampled recordings combined into one work, such as one record's vocal over another's music.
A section of a record set to repeat.
A recording cut into pieces and played back in a new order.
A sample changed enough to do a job its makers never planned.
The drum-led passage of a record that dancers waited for; looping it by hand on two turntables is where hip-hop DJing starts.
Kool Herc's name for cutting from break to break on two turntables.
Music composed from recorded real-world sounds, begun by Pierre Schaeffer in Paris in 1948.
An instrument such as the Chamberlin or Mellotron in which each key plays a strip of pre-recorded tape for about eight seconds.
John Oswald's 1985 term for making new pieces from recognizable existing recordings, with the sources credited.
A Jamaican remix of an existing track: vocal out, bass and drums forward, echo and reverb added.
The instrumental or dub cut of a song, usually on the B-side of a Jamaican single.
The stripped drum-and-bass backing track that many different songs are voiced over.
A one-off acetate disc cut for a sound system to play.
A Jamaican deejay talking or chanting over a version.
The Fairlight's stock stab of a full orchestra, taken from a recording of Stravinsky's "Firebird"; heard on "Planet Rock".
The four-bar drum solo by Gregory Coleman on the Winstons' "Amen, Brother" (1969), the drum loop under most jungle and drum and bass.
Hip-hop built on sped-up, high-pitched soul vocal samples, at its peak in the early to mid-2000s.
The beat from DJ Battery Brain's 1988 Los Angeles 12-inch "8 Volt Mix" that became the base rhythm of 1990s funk carioca.
An internet-born style, from about 2010, made by slowing and looping 1980s and 1990s pop, ads and hold music.
